# Split a String in Balanced Strings.

@example Cut after the 2nd and the 4th letter: LR, RL and LLRR each have as many Ls as Rs.
"LRRLLLRR"
=> 3

@example Every shorter beginning of s has more Rs than Ls, so the first piece can only be all of s.
"RRLRLL"
=> 1

@example Cut in the middle: LLRR and RRLL. Neither half can be cut again.
"LLRRRRLL"
=> 2

# The shortest strings.
"LR"
=> 1

"RL"
=> 1

# Pieces starting with either letter in one string: LLRR, RL and LR.
"LLRRRLLR"
=> 3

# Every pair of letters is a piece, in both orders.
"RLLRLRRL"
=> 4

# Pieces of different lengths: LR, LLRR, RRLL and LR.
"LRLLRRRRLLLR"
=> 4

# One piece in which the letters change six times: counting the places
# where neighbouring letters differ overcounts.
"LLRLRLRR"
=> 1

# One piece starting with R, three deep.
"RRRLLRLL"
=> 1

# One L, then 300 times LR, then one R: the letters keep changing, but the
# difference is back to 0 only at the very end.
""
=> 1

# 500 Ls, then 500 Rs: the difference reaches -500, past what a signed
# char holds.
""
=> 1

# 500 Rs, then 500 Ls: the difference reaches +500.
""
=> 1

# 500 pieces RL, the largest answer: past what an 8-bit count holds.
""
=> 500

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"RLLRLRRRLLRLLR"
=> 6

@gen 3 small
"LLRRRRRLLLLRRLLR"
=> 5

@gen 5 small
"LRLRLRLLRRRL"
=> 5

@gen 7 small
"LLRLRLLRLRRR"
=> 1

@gen 8 small
"RRLLLRLLLRRRRL"
=> 4

@gen 10 small
"LRRLLRLRLRLRRLRL"
=> 8

@gen 16 small
"LLLLLLRRRRRR"
=> 1

# Full-size random cases, 1000 letters: shuffled, then one piece.
@gen 3
""
=> 39

@gen 5
""
=> 1
